searches.reason: Develop controlled probes that test whether rankings depend on recent, repeated interests or broad historical associations. Compare paired history perturbations against popularity and item-frequency controls, using held-out training suffixes. Connect failures to position encoding, sequence aggregation, and recency weighting; treat perturbation effects as sensitivity evidence rather than causal proof.

searches.reason: Build a feedback-grounded audit distinguishing immediate relevance, broad relatedness, explicit compatibility conflicts, possible redundancy, and insufficient evidence. Use only histories, titles, descriptions, timestamps, and available feedback; validate labels on the twenty-user panel, report counts and abstentions, and avoid inferring ownership satisfaction or unobserved preferences. Explore how reliable error groups motivate hard-negative sampling or temporal training changes.
